sentences.display: A popular identification is a story that people choose to tell.
sentences.tts: A popular identification is a story that people choose to tell.

sentences.display: An archaeological interpretation is an argument from evidence.
sentences.tts: An archaeological interpretation is an argument from evidence.

sentences.display: An established conclusion is what remains when the arguments have been tested.
sentences.tts: An established conclusion is what remains when the arguments have been tested.

sentences.display: The link between Shisr and Iram has never moved beyond the first.
sentences.tts: The link between Shisr and إِرَم has never moved beyond the first.

sentences.display: The Quran's account of how ʿĀd came to an end is brief, and vivid.
sentences.tts: The Quran's account of how عَاد came to an end is brief, and vivid.

sentences.display: They demanded the punishment they had been warned of.
sentences.tts: They demanded the punishment they had been warned of.

sentences.display: And then, the text says,
sentences.tts: And then, the text says,

sentences.display: "when they beheld it as a dense cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: Here is a cloud bringing us rain.
sentences.tts: when they beheld it as a dense cloud coming toward their valleys, they said: Here is a cloud bringing us rain.

sentences.display: Nay, but it is that which ye did seek to hasten, a wind wherein is painful torment, destroying all things by commandment of its Lord.
sentences.tts: Nay, but it is that which ye did seek to hasten, a wind wherein is painful torment, destroying all things by commandment of its Lord.

sentences.display: And morning found them so that naught could be seen save their dwellings."
sentences.tts: And morning found them so that naught could be seen save their dwellings.

sentences.display: Elsewhere the wind is called ṣarṣar, raging, or roaring, and al-ʿaqīm, the barren wind.
sentences.tts: Elsewhere the wind is called sarsar, raging, or roaring, and al-aqeem, the barren wind.

sentences.display: It blew, the Quran says, "for seven long nights and eight long days".
sentences.tts: It blew, the Quran says, for seven long nights and eight long days.

sentences.display: Hūd, and those who believed with him, were saved.
sentences.tts: Hood, and those who believed with him, were saved.

sentences.display: The memory of that wind stayed with the Prophet Muhammad.
sentences.tts: The memory of that wind stayed with the Prophet Muhammad.

sentences.display: His wife ʿĀʾisha reported that whenever he saw clouds or wind, concern showed on his face.
sentences.tts: His wife Aa-isha reported that whenever he saw clouds or wind, concern showed on his face.

sentences.display: When she asked him why, he said that a people had been punished with wind, and that when they saw it coming, they had said, "This cloud will give us rain."
sentences.tts: When she asked him why, he said that a people had been punished with wind, and that when they saw it coming, they had said, This cloud will give us rain.

sentences.display: نُصِرْتُ بِالصَّبَا، وَأُهْلِكَتْ عَادٌ بِالدَّبُورِ
sentences.tts: نُصِرْتُ بِالصَّبَا، وَأُهْلِكَتْ عَادٌ بِالدَّبُورْ

sentences.display: In another authentic report, he said: "I was granted victory with the east wind, and ʿĀd were destroyed by the west wind."
sentences.tts: In another authentic report, he said: I was granted victory with the east wind, and عَاد were destroyed by the west wind.

sentences.display: Science cannot test a religious account of divine judgement.
sentences.tts: Science cannot test a religious account of divine judgement.

sentences.display: But it can ask a different question: how has this land itself changed?
sentences.tts: But it can ask a different question: how has this land itself changed?

sentences.display: In a cave called Qunf, in the mountains of Dhofar, a stalagmite has recorded rainfall for thousands of years, layer by layer.
sentences.tts: In a cave called Qunf, in the mountains of Dhofar, a stalagmite has recorded rainfall for thousands of years, layer by layer.

sentences.display: A study published in two thousand and three found that monsoon rain here was stronger in the early Holocene, and that after about eight thousand years ago, it gradually declined.
sentences.tts: A study published in two thousand and three found that monsoon rain here was stronger in the early Holocene, and that after about eight thousand years ago, it gradually declined.

sentences.display: Deep in the Rubʿ al-Khālī, researchers reported in two thousand and twenty-five that, during an ancient humid phase, heavy rains filled a lake of about eleven hundred square kilometres, which eventually broke its banks and carved a valley some one hundred and fifty kilometres long.
sentences.tts: Deep in the Rub al Khaali, researchers reported in two thousand and twenty-five that, during an ancient humid phase, heavy rains filled a lake of about eleven hundred square kilometres, which eventually broke its banks and carved a valley some one hundred and fifty kilometres long.

sentences.display: Arabia, in other words, was not always this dry.
sentences.tts: Arabia, in other words, was not always this dry.

sentences.display: Over many thousands of years, its landscapes have shifted between green and gold.
sentences.tts: Over many thousands of years, its landscapes have shifted between green and gold.

sentences.display: But we should be clear.
sentences.tts: But we should be clear.

sentences.display: These changes unfolded over centuries and millennia.
sentences.tts: These changes unfolded over centuries and millennia.

sentences.display: No study has dated the people of ʿĀd, and no geological event has been shown to match the Quranic account.
sentences.tts: No study has dated the people of عَاد, and no geological event has been shown to match the Quranic account.

sentences.display: At Shisr, the excavators found no evidence that a sandstorm destroyed the site.
sentences.tts: At Shisr, the excavators found no evidence that a sandstorm destroyed the site.

sentences.display: The collapse of its fortress into a sinkhole has a geological explanation, and no known connection to ʿĀd.
sentences.tts: The collapse of its fortress into a sinkhole has a geological explanation, and no known connection to عَاد.

sentences.display: Religious memory and physical evidence are answering different questions.
sentences.tts: Religious memory and physical evidence are answering different questions.

sentences.display: Merging them would do justice to neither.
sentences.tts: Merging them would do justice to neither.

sentences.display: In recent years, the search for Iram has taken an unexpected turn, away from the southern sands altogether.
sentences.tts: In recent years, the search for إِرَم has taken an unexpected turn, away from the southern sands altogether.

sentences.display: In the deserts of southern Jordan lies Wadi Ramm, the valley known today as Wadi Rum: red cliffs, and some twenty thousand recorded inscriptions.
sentences.tts: In the deserts of southern Jordan lies Wadi Ramm, the valley known today as Wadi Rum: red cliffs, and some twenty thousand recorded inscriptions.

sentences.display: A Nabataean temple to the goddess Allat stands at the foot of Jabal Ramm, and inscriptions from the site give the ancient name of the place as Iram.
sentences.tts: A Nabataean temple to the goddess Allat stands at the foot of Jabal Ramm, and inscriptions from the site give the ancient name of the place as إِرَم.

sentences.display: In two thousand and twenty-five, the epigrapher Ahmad Al-Jallad published a study of pre-Islamic inscriptions written by members of a tribe called ʿĀd, in the deserts of the north, and argued that the Quranic names may belong to this region.
sentences.tts: In two thousand and twenty-five, the epigrapher Ahmad Al-Jallad published a study of pre-Islamic inscriptions written by members of a tribe called عَاد, in the deserts of the north, and argued that the Quranic names may belong to this region.

sentences.display: It is a serious proposal, built on careful readings of ancient texts.
sentences.tts: It is a serious proposal, built on careful readings of ancient texts.

sentences.display: It is also new, and scholars are still weighing it.
sentences.tts: It is also new, and scholars are still weighing it.

sentences.display: Like Shisr before it, it shows how much depends on the evidence we choose to follow.
sentences.tts: Like Shisr before it, it shows how much depends on the evidence we choose to follow.

sentences.display: So, what can we actually say?
sentences.tts: So, what can we actually say?

sentences.display: The Quran tells of a people named ʿĀd; of their prophet, Hūd; of their strength and their building; and of a wind that left only their dwellings.
sentences.tts: The Quran tells of a people named عَاد; of their prophet, Hood; of their strength and their building; and of a wind that left only their dwellings.

sentences.display: It names Iram once, and calls it dhāt al-ʿimād.
sentences.tts: It names إِرَم once, and calls it dhaat al-ee-maad.

sentences.display: The classical scholars recorded a debate.
sentences.tts: The classical scholars recorded a debate.

sentences.display: Two of the most influential, al-Ṭabarī and Ibn Kathīr, understood Iram as a tribe, and its ʿimād as the poles of tents.
sentences.tts: Two of the most influential, al-Tabari and Ibn Katheer, understood إِرَم as a tribe, and its ee-maad as the poles of tents.

sentences.display: And they rejected the legend of a golden city.
sentences.tts: And they rejected the legend of a golden city.

sentences.display: Archaeology has found real places: a caravan fortress at Shisr, frankincense ports on the coast, and, in the north, inscriptions that name both Iram and a tribe called ʿĀd.
sentences.tts: Archaeology has found real places: a caravan fortress at Shisr, frankincense ports on the coast, and, in the north, inscriptions that name both إِرَم and a tribe called عَاد.

sentences.display: It has not found a city of a thousand pillars.
sentences.tts: It has not found a city of a thousand pillars.

sentences.display: And some things remain unknown: when ʿĀd lived; exactly where; and what their pillars really were.
sentences.tts: And some things remain unknown: when عَاد lived; exactly where; and what their pillars really were.

sentences.display: Perhaps that is the real lesson of Iram.
sentences.tts: Perhaps that is the real lesson of إِرَم.

sentences.display: A people can survive in memory long after their stones are gone, or even if they never built in stone at all.
sentences.tts: A people can survive in memory long after their stones are gone, or even if they never built in stone at all.

sentences.display: A few words in a sacred text have outlived empires, maps and explorers.
sentences.tts: A few words in a sacred text have outlived empires, maps and explorers.

sentences.display: The wind still moves across the sand, as it always has, erasing footprints by evening.
sentences.tts: The wind still moves across the sand, as it always has, erasing footprints by evening.

sentences.display: What remains is the question.
sentences.tts: What remains is the question.

sentences.display: And the discipline to tell the difference between what we know, what we believe, and what we only imagine.
sentences.tts: And the discipline to tell the difference between what we know, what we believe, and what we only imagine.
